text: This UPS driver just made three right turns... to avoid ONE left.
Sounds ridiculous, right?
But there's a reason.
Meet Mike. He's got a truck full of packages and a computer-planned route.
He spots a shortcut.
One left turn. Straight to the next delivery.
Easy.
Except... the traffic doesn't stop.
Cars keep coming.
His engine keeps running.
And Mike? He's going nowhere.
That's why UPS factors left turns into its route calculations.
An unnecessary left can get a twenty-second penalty in UPS's route math.
Not for the driver. For the route.
So sometimes, three right turns beat one left.
And here's the crazy part.
MythBusters actually tested this with a delivery truck.
Their right-turn route was LONGER.
But it used less fuel.
And every mile counts. UPS says cutting just one mile per driver, per day, can save up to fifty million dollars a year.
So UPS doesn't ban left turns.
If turning left makes more sense, the system can choose it.
So Mike wasn't taking the long way by mistake.
He was taking the smarter way.
Because in delivery...
The shortest route isn't always the cheapest.
